findings.description: The gate keeps an `authoritative` mode that trusts `tool_input.active_skill` from the PreToolUse payload. The new header comment itself states the harness sets no skill field and `tool_input` is model-authored. Once an operator sets `implement_gate.mode: authoritative` in .loa.config.yaml, the model can include `"active_skill": "implement"` in any Write/Edit call and the App-Zone fence treats the write as gated, removing the fail-ask prompt. The change removes auto-enablement via platform-features.json (good) but leaves the bypass primitive reachable through a single config key with no warning that the mode is unsound.
findings.failure_mode: An agent writing application code outside /implement or /bug self-asserts the skill in tool_input and the C-PROC-001 fence silently allows the write whenever the operator has enabled authoritative mode.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the authoritative branch (or make it a no-op that logs and falls through to the heuristic) until the harness supplies a field the model cannot author. If kept, emit a WARN on every invocation that authoritative mode is model-trusting, and never let `tool_input.active_skill` downgrade a fail-ask to allow.

findings.cross_file_justification: .claude/defaults/model-config.yaml (diff-touched) places anthropic:claude-headless as the terminal fallback hop for claude-opus-5-5 (line 489) and the existing Opus 5 / Fable 5.1 chains; the row's notes say catalog `extra.allowed_tools` widens the CLI's tools, but nothing in the registry or the new parity test (test_trust_scopes.py) binds the declared capabilities to that catalog field.
findings.description: The new registry row declares claude-headless as `execution_mode: remote_model` with file_read/file_write/command_execution/network_access all false. It is actually a local `claude -p` subprocess running under the operator's subscription in the project directory; its effective tool surface is decided by the catalog's `extra.allowed_tools`, which the row only mentions in prose. Every HTTP model's fallback chain now terminates in this hop, so an HTTP outage silently moves review/red-team/flatline traffic from a side-effect-free remote API to a local process whose capabilities the trust registry does not verify.
findings.failure_mode: An operator widens `extra.allowed_tools` for an interactive use case; later an API-side failure demotes an automated review or red-team hop onto claude-headless, which now has Write/Bash on the operator's checkout while the registry still reports a no-capability remote model.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test (alongside test_every_anthropic_catalog_entry_has_a_row) asserting that if `providers.anthropic.models.claude-headless.extra.allowed_tools` is non-empty, the registry row's capabilities are not all false, or have the headless adapter refuse to start with a non-empty allowed_tools when invoked as a fallback hop. Label execution_mode for CLI hops distinctly (e.g. local_cli) so the parity test can enforce the stricter contract.

findings.description: `rule_key` returns 1 for any rule that is not `Bash(...)`, which silently drops non-Bash allow/deny rules (Read, Edit, WebFetch(domain:…)) from both maps. In the requirement loop at line 235 `rule_key "$perm"` is called without `|| ...` under `set -euo pipefail`, so a non-Bash entry in `all_required` aborts the whole preflight instead of reporting it. The grammar also asserts `Bash(cmd *)` and `Bash(cmd:*)` are equivalent wildcards; if the harness treats the space form differently, the checker reports a permission as present (or a deny as covering) when the runtime disagrees.
findings.failure_mode: A deny rule written in a non-Bash or glob form is ignored by the checker, so a preflight passes while the runtime prompts or denies; or a non-Bash required rule crashes the checker on every preflight.
findings.suggested_fix: Handle `rule_key` failure explicitly in the requirement loop (`rule_key "$perm" || { warn ...; continue; }`), key non-Bash rules by their exact text instead of dropping them, and add a bats case pinning the `:*` vs ` *` equivalence against the documented Claude Code grammar.

findings.cross_file_justification: .claude/adapters/tests/test_max_tokens_defaults.py (diff-touched) pins the new behaviour: non-Anthropic providers default to min(16000, catalog max_output_tokens) instead of 4096, but its cost-ceiling table (test_worst_case_output_cost_per_call_is_bounded) iterates only providers.anthropic.models.
findings.description: The help text and tests document a 4x increase in the default output budget for every non-Anthropic provider (openai, google, xai, bedrock, cursor). The only cost-ceiling regression test covers Anthropic entries, so the cost exposure of the new default on e.g. gpt-5.5-pro or gemini-3.1-pro-preview is unmeasured. The flatline/red-team dispatchers fan out to several of these models per run.
findings.failure_mode: A runaway multi-model flatline or red-team run now burns up to 16K output tokens per non-Anthropic hop by default with no pinned per-call ceiling, quadrupling worst-case spend without an operator decision.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the per-call cost-ceiling test to every http_api entry across all providers and pin a maximum worst_default_micro, or keep bounded dispatchers (flatline, dissent, BB) on an explicit max_tokens.

findings.cross_file_justification: The schema added in this diff (.claude/data/schemas/model-config-v3.schema.json, probed_ceiling) defines the field as 'the last measured input bound'; the supplied full-file test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py asserts claude-opus-5-5 is calibrated and a foreign-transport entry, which the diff's catalog (calibrated_at: null, source: conservative_default) contradicts.
findings.description: `probed_ceiling: 180000` is written for Opus 5.5 while the inline comment admits it was never probed on 5.5; `routing/ceiling.input_bound` consumes this field for uncalibrated entries, so an enforcement-critical gate value is carrying borrowed provenance. Separately, the escalated full-file test module expects 5.5 to be calibrated with probed_headless provenance, so either the test or the catalog is out of step with the state this diff ships.
findings.failure_mode: The input-ceiling gate admits requests up to a bound measured on a different model; if 5.5's real accept is lower, hops fail at the provider instead of being routed down, and the catalog's provenance fields misreport why.
findings.suggested_fix: Either omit probed_ceiling for 5.5 (letting the policy use the conservative cap with honest provenance) or record it under an explicit `source: borrowed_from: claude-opus-5` marker, and reconcile the catalog with the cycle-127 test expectations before merging.
